title: RBAC v2 migration: dual-write reconcile and attenuated rollback plan with audit-grade logging
creator: Priya Rao
description: Goal: Safely migrate tenant and org role mappings from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with zero data loss, provable audit trails, and an attenuated rollback plan that minimizes customer disruption. This ticket covers: (1) dual-write strategy implementation and monitoring, (2) backfill reconciliation jobs, (3) audit-log parity checks and retention/consistency verification, (4) staged cutover and canary policy, and (5) admin/operator rollback and communication playbook. Primary acceptance targets are >99.99% mapping parity during dual-write, end-to-end audit event coverage for every principal change, and automated rollback triggers tied to SLO breaches.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dual-write enabled for 30% of traffic with reconciliation showing <0.01% uncompensated diffs over 72h; 2) Backfill job completes for historical 24 months of role events with zero gated failures; 3) Audit log parity validated (event idempotency + ordering) and archived to customer-auditable store; 4) Cutover runbook and rollback steps fleshed out, dry-run completed by SRE and Security; 5) Customer notification templates and per-customer opt-out automation exist.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs considered: 1) Strong immediate cutover vs. phased dual-write: phased dual-write chosen to preserve availability and allow reconciliation; 2) Synchronous write to v2 for all ops would simplify correctness but increase latency and coupling — we limit synchronous writes to admin-boundary changes during canary; 3) Keeping v1 as read fallback vs. promoting v2 reads incrementally: promoting v2 reads by route with per-tenant opt-in reduces long-term dual-read complexity at cost of more fine-grained rollout logic. We will accept a small window of eventual consistency during backfill in exchange for predictable latency and rollback ability.
security_considerations: All dual-write traffic is encrypted and signed; audit events include correlation id, actor, source route, and version. KMS integration required for archival encryption. Security to review retention policy for customer-facing audit exports. Admin RBAC controls must be preserved across both stores to avoid privilege drift.
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (prework): schema validation, test fixtures, and canonical role model doc (done). Phase 1 (dual-write core): implement dual-write library, idempotency keys, and per-tenant feature flags. Phase 2 (observability): publish consistency metrics, error budgets, and alert burn rate dashboards. Phase 3 (backfill): run windowed backfill jobs with throttling and checkpointing. Phase 4 (canary reads & cutover): enable v2 reads for internal tenants, then 5% external tenants, monitor for 72h; if stable, accelerate. Phase 5 (deprecate v1): after 30d stable, schedule v1 read-deprecation with customer notices.
rollback_plan_high_level: Automated rollback triggers: sustained inconsistency >0.05% over 1h, elevated 500s/latency for admin operations, or loss of audit integrity. Rollback steps: (1) pause dual-write and drain queues; (2) switch reads back to v1 using traffic-routing feature flag; (3) run quick reconciliation job marking v2 writes as pending for manual review; (4) notify customers and Ops. Rollback dry-run performed in staging 2025-12-18.
communication_plan: Week -3: Heads-up email to affected customers and internal SEs; Week -1: Detailed migration timeline + per-tenant opt-in instructions; Day 0: Migration start broadcast with status link; Post migration: summary report + audit export availability. Customer templates stored in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/security/rbac-v2-comms.
postmortem_and_metrics: If any rollback occurs or parity >0.1% observed, author a postmortem within 72h. Key metrics: parity_rate, backfill_errors_per_minute, audit_delivery_lag_ms, admin_op_latency_p99, number_of_affected_customers.
